issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Lemma 3, dividing on the left by generalized Bézout's theorem produces successive factors to the right of earlier ones, yielding the product (\lambda I - \widehat{B}_d)(\lambda I - \widehat{B}_{d-1})\dots(\lambda I - \widehat{B}_2)\Phi_0 with descending indices from left to right. Because matrix multiplication does not commute, this is not equal to the ascending product \prod_{i=2}^d (\lambda I - \widehat{B}_i) = (\lambda I - \widehat{B}_2)\dots(\lambda I - \widehat{B}_d) stated in (2.7). Moreover, equation (2.10) incorrectly multiplies \omega_i^\Ttran by the leftmost factor as if it were (\lambda_i I - \widehat{B}_{i+1}), and the forward recurrence for S_{i,j} (with j running from i+1 to d) does not match the evaluation at B_1 of either product. As a result, for d >= 3, the formula fails to define a fundamental matrix polynomial: for example, taking d=3, b=2 with B_3 = diag(1, 2) and B_2 = [3, 1; 0, 4] gives \Phi(B_3) = [0, 0.5; 0, 0] S_{1,3}^{-1} \neq 0 and \Phi(B_2) \neq 0 instead of vanishing at B_2 and B_3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the order of the linear factors in the product to (\lambda I - \widehat{B}_d)(\lambda I - \widehat{B}_{d-1})\dots(\lambda I - \widehat{B}_2) S^{-1}, and redefine the recurrence for S_{i,j} to apply \widehat{B}_d first and proceed backward down to \widehat{B}_{i+1}, properly matching the left multiplication in the induction and the evaluation at B_1.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit factorization of fundamental matrix polynomials in Lemma 3 and Theorem 1 is invalid for d >= 3. Consequently, Proposition 3, the growth bound (2.13) in Theorem 2, the structural bound in Theorem 3, and the definitions of chi_mono and chi_coef underlying Conjecture 1 and its Corollary are unsupported as stated.
issues.title: Invalid factor ordering and recurrence in the explicit formula for fundamental matrix polynomials
issues.why_classification: The error stems from non-commutativity in the matrix polynomial factorization. A contained repair that reverses the indexing of the recurrence and the linear factor ordering restores the fundamental matrix polynomials and preserves all subsequent theorems, bounds, and advertised rates without requiring new global architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: In the definition of c_Omega, the norm term \max_{d+1\le j\le m} \|\Omega_j\| appears squared. Squaring c_Omega therefore raises this norm term to the fourth power, (\max_{d+1\le j\le m} \|\Omega_j\|)^4. Applying the standard Gaussian norm tail bound should produce a factor of (2\sqrt{b} + \sqrt{2\log(2(m-d)/\delta)})^4. The bound stated in Theorem 3 includes this term only to the first power, which renders the bound mathematically false in regimes where 2\sqrt{b} is large. Furthermore, the proof quotes the tail bound as \sqrt{2\log(\delta/2)}, which is ill-defined (negative under the square root) for \delta < 1, rather than \sqrt{2\log(2/\delta)}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first power of (2\sqrt{b} + \sqrt{2\log(2(m-d)/\delta)}) in the high-probability bound for c_Omega^2 with the fourth power, and correct \sqrt{2\log(\delta/2)} to \sqrt{2\log(2/\delta)} in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The high-probability upper bound on c_Omega^2 in Theorem 3 is incorrect as stated and underestimates the true tail bound by three powers of (2\sqrt{b} + \sqrt{2\log(2(m-d)/\delta)}).
issues.title: Incorrect power on norm bound in tail probability estimate for c_Omega^2
issues.why_classification: Restoring the correct exponent 4 and fixing the inverted fraction inside the logarithm is a routine local correction that leaves the proof architecture, structural bound, and all main qualitative conclusions intact.
